entities.summary: Franz Sznayde was a Polish senior military officer who played a crucial role in the defense of Warsaw against Napoleon's forces in 1812. Born around 1795, he rose through the ranks to become a brigadier general by 1820 and led several successful campaigns against Russian and Prussian forces. Sznayde's leadership during this period helped to secure Poland's independence from foreign rule and cement his legacy as one of the most important military leaders in Polish history. He died on December 13, 1850, at the age of 55, leaving behind a reputation for bravery, strategic genius, and unwavering dedication to his country.
